meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the MEA-CO2 unit
meta.scope: From the DCC outlet (flue gas battery limit) through the absorber T-101, the solvent circuit and the stripper T-102 to the stack and the CO2 battery limit, including utilities (LP steam, cooling water, demin make-up water, instrument air, electrical power).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. LP steam, cooling water, demin water, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
K-101 motor trip
VFD failure
XV-101 spurious closure
FIC-101 transmitter fails high (speed cut back)
N1.cons: No CO2 captured: the whole slip-stream CO2 goes to the stack. The stripper keeps steaming with no CO2 load (over-stripping, steam wasted, overhead hot).

N1.causes:
Power-plant load push: FIC-101 set point raised
FIC-101 transmitter reads low
Set-point error
N1.cons: L/G falls and capture drops below 90 %; T-101 approaches flood, ΔP and liquid entrainment to the wash and stack rise (amine emission); K-101 power rises.

N1.dev: High pressure at the T-101 gas inlet
N1.causes:
Absorber flooding or plugged packing/demister
K-101 at high speed against a restriction
N1.cons: Duct and expansion joints over-pressured; flue gas (low O2, CO, NOx) leaks at grade — asphyxiation hazard; T-101 shell above its low design pressure.

N1.dev: Reverse flow from T-101 into the duct and blower
N1.causes:
K-101 trips with XV-101 still open (XV-101 closes only on I-1)
T-101 sump level up to the gas inlet
N1.cons: Wet, amine-laden gas or liquid amine back into the blower casing and duct: corrosion, liquid slug and blower damage on restart, amine spill at duct drains.

N1.dev: More CO2 in the flue gas
N1.causes: Gas turbine at part load / duct firing: CO2 up to 6 mol%
N1.cons: Rich loading rises (corrosion of the hot rich side), capture falls unless the lean rate and steam follow.

sg.text: LSHH-109 90 % → I-1 unit trip: K-101 stop, XV-101 and XV-207 shut (5 s)
Procedure: raise FIC-201 and keep TIC-206 (OTS procedure)

recs.text: Write and train a loss-of-flue-gas response (K-101 trip): cut the steam to hot standby, keep the solvent circulating and the overhead in AUTO.
Close XV-101 (or fit a non-return damper) when K-101 stops, not only on I-1.
Add an L/G ratio (lean set point from the measured flue gas) with high and low limits, and an operator guide for CO2 changes.
Add a flood override: on PDI-102 or AY-102 high-high, hold or cut back the FIC-101 set point automatically.
Show the T-101 inlet pressure (PI-101, in the DCS) on CC-PID-101 with a high alarm; confirm duct and T-101 design pressure against the K-101 shut-off head.
